gate: ADOPT the tuned-Elo spec if grid-tuned K + HFA + regression-to-mean beats the paper's fixed recipe (init 1500, K=25, no HFA) by >=0.005 mean log-loss on 2020-2025, with a Brier-score improvement in the same direction; REJECT if the tuned variant fails to beat the fixed recipe.

title: The SIDO Performance Model for League of Legends
improvement: Own/ally/enemy attribution for NFL skill positions on nflverse play-by-play: own model - e.g. WR yards/route = beta_0 + b_scheme + b_player + epsilon (scheme/team random effect analogous to champion); ally model - residualize teammates' production (other WRs' yards, RB efficiency) and model the sum of residuals on the player; enemy model - e.g. pass-rusher's effect on opposing QB EPA (metric = -b_p); start with QBs (effect on teammates' EPA) and edge rushers (effect on opponent dropback EPA); adopt the Franks et al. meta-metrics as GSE's metric-QC gate: every new advanced metric must report discrimination (signal vs sampling noise), independence (new information vs existing metrics, Gaussian copula), stability (concordance across season halves); honesty rule: low-discrimination components get bucketed into categories, not published as continuous rankings - plus per-teammate-pair effects: fit QB->specific-WR chemistry as a random interaction rather than one pooled ally effect, testing whether QB-WR pair effects predict next-season performance of reunited pairs (a 'stack' signal for DFS/betting grounded in the SIDO framework).
gate: Adopt the attribution framework if the own-effect model beats raw EPA/dropback on out-of-sample prediction RMSE (train 2020-2023, predict 2024-2025 player efficiency) AND achieves discrimination >=0.5 with stability concordance >=0.6; reject ally/enemy continuous scores if their discrimination <0.3: bucket them into the 5 categories instead of publishing numbers.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
improvement: Chronos for NFL team margins: (1) baseline experiment - zero-shot Chronos-T5-Small/Base on weekly NFL team-margin series (2002-2024), score WQL/MASE vs the engine's current margins; (2) sports adaptation - fine-tune Chronos-T5-Small on GSE's sports corpus (team margins, totals, player usage) using the paper's recipe (AdamW, low LR, early stopping on seasonal holdout); use sampled paths as the probabilistic engine input for spread/total pricing; (3) covariate extension: adopt ChronosX (ledger 2127) adapters on top of the fine-tuned Chronos to inject weather, rest, injuries - do not reinvent covariate handling; (4) serving: batch-infer quantile paths per game, feed WQL-calibrated distributions to the moneyline/CLV pricing layer - plus a tokenization resolution study: re-quantize with finer vocab (8192 bins) or learned quantization on sports series, measuring whether sub-point precision (matters for key numbers 3/7) improves WQL, combined with a mean-scale replacement (robust scale = median absolute deviation).
gate: ADOPT into the engine's probabilistic path if fine-tuned Chronos beats the engine's current margin MAE by >=0.3 points AND its WQL is <=0.95x the SeasonalNaive baseline on 2021-2024; ADAPT (keep researching) if it only matches; REJECT the covariate-free variant for live pricing if WQL does not beat naive; hard reject if any sample-path distribution fails a calibration check (empirical coverage of 80% intervals deviates >5 pts from nominal).

title: MambaMOT: State-Space Model as Motion Predictor for Multi-Object Tracking
improvement: Tracking-upgrade lane shared with ledger 0063 (MambaTrack): defer to 0063's bidirectional predictor for the motion model itself (it beats MambaMOT on SportsMOT, 72.6 vs 71.3 HOTA); the marginal contribution worth taking from MambaMOT is the cheap O(N) tracklet-merging head via trajectory embeddings - directly useful for stitching fragmented player tracklets across broadcast camera cuts and occlusion-heavy pile-ups; build plan: implement the Mamba motion predictor per the mamba-ssm reference (input [x,y,w,h] box history -> linear lift -> 2 Mamba blocks -> MLP heads for box prediction and trajectory embedding); train on GSE-labeled broadcast tracking (SportsMOT as a warm start); plug into a ByteTrack-style association loop replacing the Kalman predict step; add the post-hoc hierarchical-clustering merge (cosine on embeddings, 50-frame/50-pixel veto gates tuned to football); benchmark IDF1/HOTA against the current Kalman baseline - plus fuse the trajectory embedding with an appearance (jersey-number) embedding, tune merge thresholds to football with a shot-boundary-aware merge gate, and extend predictor input to full NGS-style state (velocity, orientation).
gate: ADOPT the merging head only if tracklet fragmentation drops >= 20% at equal-or-better IDF1 vs Kalman; ADOPT the motion predictor only if it beats 0063 head-to-head on HOTA; latency must clear >= 25 FPS; if none hold, REJECT and defer to 0063.

title: Comprehensive OOS Evaluation of Predictive Algorithms with Statistical Decision Theory
improvement: As engine-honesty infrastructure, adopt minimax-regret (MMR) engine selection: define the state space S = (training-era, prediction-era) pairs (e.g. train 2019-2022 -> predict 2023) plus stressed states (post-rule-change seasons, QB-injury clusters, weather-extreme slates); define the SDF: c(.) = [data -> GSE probabilities -> bet/no-bet + stake rule]; loss = negative bankroll log-growth (or negative CLV) per slate; compute regret per state: for each candidate engine variant (v5.2.7 vs challengers), Monte-Carlo over bootstrap resamples of the training era -> expected loss, regret = expected loss - best-variant loss in that state; report maximum regret across S alongside the usual average backtest; prefer the engine with small maximum regret ('uniformly near-optimal') over the one with the best average but a catastrophic regime - plus make the state space adversarial: an automated 'regime generator' searching over plausible perturbations (injury rates, line-shading shifts, weather distributions) for the state maximizing each engine's regret - max regret by optimization rather than a hand-picked grid.
gate: Adopt MMR as a standing engine-selection criterion if the max-regret ranking disagrees with the average-backtest ranking on at least one real engine decision in 2024-2025 (it changes a choice we would otherwise make) - that demonstrates the doctrine adds information; if max-regret and average-backtest always agree, keep reporting MMR as a diagnostic but do not let it override averages.

title: Benchmarking Badminton Action Recognition with a New Fine-Grained Dataset
improvement: Adopt the architecture-selection ladder for GSE's video action-recognition lane: reproduce the paper's ranking (ST-GCN/PoseC3D top at 10-50 shots; SlowFast/Swin top at full data) and re-run the ladder with player-disjoint folds (group clips by athlete into 5 folds) to measure how much absolute accuracies drop and whether the skeleton-first ranking survives - this quantifies identity-leakage inflation and produces GSE a leak-corrected benchmark; add a VPD-style distilled-pose backbone to the ladder.
gate: The architecture-selection harness is adopted only if the reproduced ranking matches the paper's within +/-3pp - if the ranking does not reproduce, treat the paper as dataset-only and re-derive GSE's own ranking from scratch.

title: SportsNGEN: Sustained Generation of Realistic Multi-player Sports Gameplay
improvement: Build an NFL multi-player gameplay generator on NFL Next Gen Stats tracking (22 players + ball at 10 Hz, aligned to play-level outcomes: EPA, win probability added): replace tennis-specific heads (rally stopping) with play-boundary logic (whistle/end-of-play); identity embeddings per NFL player with a fallback 'generic' embedding for rookies/trades (addressing the paper's OOD weakness); grid resolution scaled to the NFL field (finer in x given yard-line value); same decoder skeleton (4-layer transformer, categorical grid offsets, nucleus sampling); add conditioning on play-call context (down, distance, formation, personnel) as context tokens for counterfactual use ('what if we blitzed / ran play-action'); per-season training with walk-forward validation across seasons; realism judged by distributional statistics of generated plays (yards gained distribution, time-to-throw) vs real tracking; offline batch counterfactual studies (100 rollouts per game-state of interest on GPU workers) - plus condition generation on defensive scheme and personnel groupings as structured context tokens (Cover-2 vs Cover-3 shell, nickel vs base), and replace the flat grid with hierarchical coarse-to-fine binning (coarse zone -> fine offset) to reduce output-head parameter count and sharpen fine field-position fidelity.
gate: Adopt the simulation lane only if BOTH hold on the Weeks 13-17 test window: (a) the decoder's generated yardage distributions achieve 1-Wasserstein distance <= 0.75x that of the Markov baseline in at least 4 of 6 play-type bins; and (b) the forced-blitz counterfactual shifts sack rate in the historically correct direction with magnitude within 50% of the observed historical blitz/non-blitz gap; reject (do not invest beyond the prototype) if either fails.

title: Offensive Lineup Analysis in Basketball with Clustering Players Based on Shooting Style and Offensive Role
improvement: Lineup role-composition features for GSE's NBA projections: recompute shooting styles (Wasserstein + Ward) and roles (fuzzy C-means) on recent seasons; for each projected lineup, emit role indicators + the top role-pair interactions as engineered features (+/-0.2-0.5 OFFRTG-scale adjustments); NGBoost (or GSE's existing probabilistic head) predicting player-level fantasy points with lineup-role features; keep the Bayesian hierarchical pair-effect estimator as an offline diagnostic; use: adjust usage/assist/points props when lineups change (injury/trade), especially for role pairs with |effect| > 0.25 - plus replace hard cluster assignments with fuzzy membership weights as continuous features, and add a scheme/team random effect to absorb the Jokic/Spurs/Warriors idiosyncrasy.
gate: ADAPT: role-composition NGBoost beats the prior-style baseline on all three metrics (RMSE 4.786 < 4.850, MAE 3.869 < 3.942, NLL 3.066 < 3.089), and the hierarchical model yields interpretable, signed pair effects up to +/-0.47; improvement success = RMSE <= 4.5 on the same lineup-prediction protocol (>= ~6% relative improvement over 4.786).

title: DAVED: Data Acquisition via Experimental Design for Data Markets
improvement: Reframe weekly model training as the data market: buyer test queries = this week's slate (unlabeled by definition - games unplayed), seller pool = historical games with charting costs c_j, budget B = weekly compute/charting dollars; features phi(x): current model embeddings (or GBM leaf-encodings / last-layer features); run FW herding (Eq. 6-8) or the single-step variant to select the training subset minimizing V-optimal proxy error on this week's slate; train the week's head on the selected subset - replacing 'train on last N weeks / all history' with 'train on the history most informative for these specific matchups' - compose with ledger 2008: the same budget B governs both training-data acquisition (DAVED) and new charting acquisition (ConBatch-BAL) - split B between them by the marginal proxy-loss reduction each buys - plus a hybrid selector: DAVED's V-optimal term for matchup-relevance plus an explicit recency prior folded into the initial weights w_0 (initialize w_0 proportional to exp(-age/tau) instead of uniform 1/n) before FW herding; tau becomes a tunable 'football memory' parameter, ablated over {4, 8, 17, 34} weeks.
gate: ADOPT DAVED-selected training sets iff they beat the recency-window baseline by >= 0.003 weekly ATS log-loss averaged over the 2024 season AND beat it in >= 10 of 18 weeks (consistency), with the win holding under both cost functions (sqrt(c), c^2); REJECT if DAVED ~= recency or if it underperforms random selection in any 4-week stretch.

title: Fractional Tackles: A New Defensive Statistic Derived from Player Tracking Data
improvement: Tracking-derived fractional tackle credit: detect contact windows (1.5-yard rule) on run plays; compute window values from a ball-carrier end-of-play model; attribute credit by peak toward-carrier velocity; aggregate per defender per game/season; outputs: per-player fractional-tackle rate (per play, per snap) -> features for IDP projections and tackle-prop pricing; first-contact share as a separate 'disruption' feature; extend to pass plays: pressure windows (distance-to-QB < threshold) with sack/throwaway value attribution - plus learn the attribution shares (gradient-boosted model predicting window value from defender kinematic features) instead of the fixed velocity rule, and extend windows to pass plays.
gate: ADAPT: split-half reliability 0.69 > 0.59 overall and better in all three position groups; 2.5x coverage (19,691 vs. 7,720 instances); public code + data; improvement success = split-half reliability >= 0.72 on run plays and >= 0.60 on pass-rush windows, with the learned shares outperforming the velocity heuristic in window-value cross-validation.

title: The Evolution of Football Betting: A Machine Learning Approach to Match Outcome Forecasting and Bookmaker Odds Estimation
improvement: As engine-honesty infrastructure, port the two empirical priors as feature-selection guidance: prioritize xG-family features (xG, xGA, SCA, GCA) at the top of GSE's NFL analog feature list (EPA, success rate, explosive-play rate - the NFL equivalents of chance-creation metrics); treat draw/no-result and tie-ish outcomes as intrinsically low-signal classes - do not over-allocate model capacity to them; for NFL this maps to not overfitting push/OT edge cases; REJECT the paper's classifiers themselves - KEEP the feature priors - plus a draw-difficulty analog: quantify the engine's current accuracy on 'coin-flip' NFL games (spread within +/-2.5) vs the rest; if coin-flip accuracy is near 50%, test whether abstaining or stake-reducing on those games improves bankroll growth under fractional Kelly - turning the paper's descriptive finding into a staking rule.
gate: If EPA-family features rank top-3 in the univariate screen, the paper's finding is confirmed as a prior and GSE's existing feature hierarchy stands - ledger closes as guidance-only; if raw yardage dominates EPA, flag a feature-engineering review.

title: Visualization of Unstructured Sports Data - An Example of Cricket Short Text Commentary
improvement: Tendency-rule miner v1: build confrontation matrices from nflverse play descriptions - rows = offensive player response features (target depth, separation proxy, YAC bucket), columns = defensive features (coverage shell, blitz, press); run correspondence analysis per player-season (>=150 routes); extract top-2 'strength' (high-success) and 'weakness' (low-success) rules as <F, G_j> argmax pairs; similar-player clustering via t-SNE/UMAP on concatenated rule vectors for comp-based DFS/prop projections (find cheap comps with the same tendency profile); validate by replicating the paper's two studies - expert check against established scouting reports, Procrustes train/test (prior season vs current season) stability - plus replace the hand-built feature taxonomy with a learned one: run a domain-tuned LLM over the raw commentary to extract (attribute, response) structured tuples, then apply CA on the learned taxonomy.
gate: ADAPT the CA rule-mining template now; ADOPT for matchup modeling only if cross-season Procrustes stability holds (median Delta^2 <= 0.35) and weakness-rule matchups predict target-share shortfalls out-of-sample; otherwise REJECT as a descriptive/visualization tool only.

title: Postprocessing point predictions for probabilistic forecasting: IDR beats DDNN
improvement: Postprocess GSE's point predictions with IDR: calibrate the engine's point forecasts into probabilistic forecasts using isotonic distributional regression, ensembled with the Gaussian-error benchmark (LEAR-N analog) - combine IDR with mAFTER-style adaptive weighting (ledger 0786) across multiple calibration windows instead of the simple vertical average, since window selection is where IDR's volatility lives (the poor Dec-2019-Apr-2021 stretch) - adaptively weighting windows should capture the upside while dampening the bad spells.
gate: CPA test: IDR-ensemble significantly outperforms Gaussian-error benchmark at 5% in both market-type subsets; Shapley contribution of IDR to the ensemble > 40%.

title: Modelling handball outcomes using univariate and bivariate approaches
improvement: ZI-Skellam2 margin model: univariate NFL margin Z (home-away points) ~ ZI-Skellam2(mu, sigma^2, p) with mu_jk = alpha + beta_j + gamma_k (team home/away abilities from nflverse 2015-2025); push handling: interpret p as excess mass at Z == spread (recenter Z' = Z - spread per game) - this converts the ZI trick from 'draws' to 'pushes', directly pricing push probability into spread bets; bivariate half model: (1H diff, 2H diff) with Skellam2 marginals + Frank copula, team abilities shared vs half-specific; output: halftime-conditional P(win), P(cover), P(over) for the live-betting surface; season sim: 10,000 Monte Carlo replications of remaining schedule for playoff-probability content - plus quarter-by-quarter vine copula: extend to four quarters with a D-vine of Frank copulas, Skellam2 marginals, abilities allowed a linear 'fatigue/adjustment' trend across quarters, testing whether NFL halves/quarters are strategically asymmetric.
gate: Adopt if ZI-Skellam2 beats plain Skellam2 by AIC >= 10 on the 2024-2025 holdout AND predicted push rate is within 0.5pp of observed AND halftime-conditional Brier beats a naive 'halftime leader wins' baseline by >=0.01; reject otherwise (fall back to the plain Skellam); the bivariate half model is adopted only if Model B (Frank, shared abilities) beats Model A (independence) by AIC >= 10.

title: X-VARS: Introducing Explainability in Football Refereeing with Multi-Modal Large Language Models
improvement: GSE 'show your work' cards: for each published pick, inject the engine's structured outputs (win prob, spread, key edges, top features) as text into a fine-tuned LLM prompt, generating a 3-5 sentence analyst-style rationale; data: GSE's historical posted picks + analyst-written rationales (X post history, weekly packets) as the explanation corpus; training: QLoRA fine-tune of an open LLM (same 1%-of-layers recipe as the paper) on (structured prediction -> rationale) pairs, plus a multi-task classification head so the model also predicts the pick, enabling the same agreement diagnostic; serving: batch generation at pick-publication time, human review before posting (fits the existing approve-desk gate) - plus a structured consistency loss: penalize the model when its generated text contradicts the injected numbers (extract numbers from generated text with regex/NER and compare to inputs).
gate: Adopt if blind mean rating >= human mean - 0.3 AND prediction-text agreement >= 90% (fixing the paper's faithfulness gap is the point); reject otherwise - a fluent but unfaithful narrator is worse than no narrator for a picks business.

title: Bunting and the ghost runner: a causal inference approach
improvement: Compact IPW template for data-vs-conventional-wisdom strategy findings, applied to NFL special teams: causal effect of fair-catching (vs returning) kickoffs on drive expected points - nflverse pbp kickoffs 2018-2024, treatment = fair catch / touchback (no return), outcome = EP of ensuing drive; confounders: returner quality, kicking-team coverage quality (DVOA-style), weather, score/time, kicker hang-time/distance; propensity: logistic/GBM; IPW with [0.1, 0.9] trimming; doubly robust (outcome regression + IPW); product: 'NFL teams are leaving points on the field by returning kickoffs' causal content + a fair-catch recommendation feature in GSE's kickoff model - plus: use Next Gen Stats returner top-speed / coverage-team closing-speed metrics as confounders the paper's box-score stats cannot capture, and run a Rosenbaum-style sensitivity analysis (absent from the paper) to report the Gamma at which the OR=1.86 finding breaks.
gate: ADAPT the IPW template if the kickoff replication achieves |SMD| < 0.1 on all confounders, propensity AUC >= 0.65, and the doubly robust EP difference has 95% CI excluding 0 with |effect| >= 0.15 EP/drive; REJECT if the CI includes 0 or the placebo punt analysis shows a 'significant' effect (residual confounding).

title: Fair Tab Diffusion: Multivariate Guidance + Balanced Sampling for Rare-Regime Synthesis
improvement: Regime-oversampling module on top of the chosen synthetic backbone (TabSyn or TabRep from ledgers 2066/2067): train the backbone generator with regime attributes included as columns (weather severity, rest days bin, prime-time, division game, dome/altitude); add multivariate classifier-free guidance head: condition on (outcome class c, regime attrs S) with the security gate (tune lambda, delta, w_s on a validation slice); balanced sampling: empirical outcome distribution x uniform regime distribution, balancing dial i in {0, 5, 10} - i=0 replicates history, i=10 uniform over regimes; generate tail-regime synthetic seasons at i=10 (e.g. 2x historical rate of severe-weather and short-rest games), mix with empirical synthetic seasons at low weight - plus a learned balancing schedule: make the balancing level a function of downstream need - i(s) per regime cell, set proportional to the current model's tail-slice calibration error on that cell (worse-calibrated cells get more synthetic mass), turning the static dial into an active-learning loop for synthetic data.
gate: ADOPT the balancing module if: (a) tail-slice log-loss improves by >=0.01 at i=10 vs i=0, AND (b) overall 2024 log-loss does not degrade by more than 0.001 vs i=0, AND (c) the security gate keeps outcome-marginal drift <=2% TVD between i=0 and i=10 samples; REJECT if any gate fails or if tuning (lambda, delta, w_s) proves unstable across 3 seeds.

title: Assumption-Lean Quantile Regression via Efficient Influence Functions
improvement: Distributional prop analysis with honest CIs: the effect of matchup/weather/rest variables on a player's yardage distribution (median vs 90th percentile), for GSE's 'most calibrated' positioning; implementation: DoubleML-style cross-fitting + TMLE fluctuation; nuisance models = gradient boosting for E(A|L) and quantile forests for Q_tau; kernel density for f(Y|.) at the quantile; start at tau in {.25, .5, .75} before attempting extremes; data: nflverse player-game features 2015-2024 - plus stabilized density estimation: replace the paper's density-at-quantile estimator with a conformalized quantile-density approach (density estimated on held-out folds with conformal cutoffs that fall back to a wider-bandwidth estimate when density < epsilon), targeting the paper's admitted near-zero-density failure mode and extending the usable tau range toward the tails.
gate: Adopt if TMLE-CF achieves 90-98% coverage with |bias| <= 25% of the plug-in's bias at tau=.5 and tau=.75 on the semi-synthetic test; reject if coverage collapses at tau=.9 (then restrict the lane to central quantiles and say so explicitly).

title: Calibrating Bayesian Learning via Regularization, Confidence Minimization, and Selective Inference
improvement: Selective calibration stack: (1) add an MMCE-style calibration regularizer to GSE's classification head loss (lambda swept on validation) - cheap, no architecture change; (2) build the selective-calibration selector: inputs = (model confidence r-bar, outlier scores vs historical game embeddings via kNN distance + isolation forest); train to minimize selective MMCE on a validation season with coverage target xi (e.g. 0.5); publish iff selector score >= tau; (3) OOD analog: treat cross-era games (e.g. pre-2020 rule changes) as the uncertainty set for confidence minimization - penalize overconfidence on era-shifted games - plus replace the paper's four hand-built outlier scores with a single learned 'game typicality' score: distance in GSE's own embedding space to the k nearest historical games, testing whether the selector's rejection decisions correlate with known hard-game indicators (backup QB, extreme weather, large line moves).
gate: ADAPT if selective calibration reduces test-window selected-set ECE by >=20% relative to the MMCE-only variant with accuracy not worse by more than 1pp; reject if the ECE gain requires >60% rejection or accuracy drops - then keep only the MMCE regularizer.

title: On Risk-Sensitive Decision Making Under Uncertainty
improvement: Per-game rho-penalized Kelly rule: for each engine pick with estimated win prob p-hat and decimal odds o, compute the rho-penalized Kelly fraction by solving the paper's optimality equation numerically (1-D root find on f(p-hat,K,rho)=0 with payoff X in {o-1,-1}) - a fractional-Kelly-like stake with rho calibrated, not an arbitrary 0.25/0.5 fraction; rho calibration: grid-search rho in [0,2] on rolling backtest to maximize Calmar ratio (not raw growth) - answering the paper's open 'how to choose rho' with data; slate extension: use the multi-alternative simplex form (each week's picks = alternatives, K = stake fractions summing to <=1, cash = deterministic alternative with r=0), payoffs correlated via historical pick-residual correlation; serving: precompute stake per pick nightly after odds sync, cap single-game stake at 3% bankroll regardless of formula output - plus make rho adaptive to bankroll state: rho_t = rho_0 x (1 + kappa*(DD_t/DD_max)), where DD_t is current drawdown - the variance penalty tightens automatically as the bankroll dips (a drawdown governor the static paper lacks).
gate: ACCEPT if on locked 2024-2025 window: Calmar_rho-Kelly >= 1.10 x Calmar_best-baseline AND max-drawdown <= 0.90 x that of full-Kelly baseline AND CAGR >= CAGR of fixed-fraction baseline; REJECT otherwise, or if optimal rho on the tuning window is 0 (then it is just Kelly) or unstable across tuning folds.

title: Conformal Predictive Systems Under Covariate Shift
improvement: Weighted conformal under covariate shift: (1) build a regime discriminator - logistic regression distinguishing 'current-regime games' (last 4 weeks) from the calibration window (trailing 2 seasons) on covariates (QB identity flags, injury counts, weather, home/away, line movement); (2) use its predicted odds as w-hat(x) in a weighted conformal interval layer for totals/spreads (via crepes-weighted or a port); (3) compare coverage/width vs unweighted rolling conformal on 2023-2025 backtests, with regime-shift weeks (starting-QB changes) flagged - plus doubly-robust CPS: combine WSCPS weighting with a conditional (Mondrian) calibration split by regime - testing whether weighting + stratification beats either alone during shift episodes.
gate: ADOPT if WSCPS restores episode-conditional coverage to within 3pp of nominal without >10% width inflation vs unweighted; REJECT if the discriminator's w-hat estimates are unstable (effective sample size of calibration < 30% of nominal - weight collapse) or if P(Y|X) drift dominates (WSCPS still miscalibrated during episodes).

title: LLM-SR: Scientific Equation Discovery via Programming with Large Language Models
improvement: Build 'GSE-SR': prompt template with (a) problem spec in analyst prose (features, target, no-known-metrics constraint listing passer rating/QBR/EPA as forbidden), (b) evaluation function code (NMSE on nflverse train + OOD future seasons), (c) one seed skeleton; LLM proposes Python skeleton programs with placeholder params; fit with scipy BFGS; score -MSE; islands-model experience buffer (m=4 islands, Boltzmann cluster sampling favoring high score + short programs); backbones: any instruction-tuned LLM (cost-controlled: batch proposals, cache); data: nflverse team-season 2009-2023 (ID), 2024-2025 (OOD); targets: points/drive, next-season wins - plus 'adversarial prior refresh': after each island converges, prompt the LLM with the current best program and explicitly instruct it to propose a structurally DIFFERENT family (e.g. 'no ratios; use only additive terms' or 'must include an interaction between pressure rate and air yards') - using the LLM's language ability as a diversity operator that GP mutation cannot provide.
gate: ADOPT if GSE-SR's best program achieves >=20% lower OOD NMSE than the best PySR expression at comparable complexity (<=15 nodes) on the 2024-2025 window AND the program is not a recitation of a known metric (verified by symbolic inspection); REJECT if OOD NMSE is within 10% of PySR or the LLM merely rediscovers passer-rating variants.

title: Cross-Block Fine-Grained Semantic Cascade for Skeleton-Based Sports Action Recognition
improvement: Add the cross-block fine-grained semantic cascade (CFSC) to GSE's skeleton-based action recognition: learn a per-level lambda_v (attention over cascade depths) instead of scalar lambda, comparing against fixed-lambda on GSE data; test CFSC on 3D skeletons (the paper used 2D OpenPose) to see if depth information reduces the bone-stream advantage.
gate: CFSC must deliver >=+1.5pp top-1 on the strong-backbone setting (the paper's own minimum on HD-GCN was +1.4 on FD-7 bone) with <=10% inference-cost increase, else drop - the value proposition is 'cheap +2pp', and anything less is not worth the module complexity.

title: BayesBlend: Bayesian Model Averaging and Stacking in Python
improvement: Adopt (or vendor-inspire) BayesBlend's Draws + stacking-model pattern as GSE's ensemble plumbing - the reference implementation candidate for the stacking lane: standardize the heterogeneous model zoo via the Draws abstraction (log-likelihood matrix + posterior predictions, first dim = posterior samples); concrete workflow: collect per-model LOO log-predictive densities -> BayesStacking (Bayesian weights with informed priors, e.g. prior preference for the production incumbent) or MleStacking for speed -> .predict produces the blended posterior-predictive Draws consumed downstream by calibration (CQR/conformal) and Kelly sizing; HierarchicalBayesStacking gives turnkey regime-dependent weights (spread bucket, dome/outdoor, week) as a Stan-backed fit rather than custom code; train blending on early weeks, apply to future weeks (leave-future-out over the season structure) - plus test backend-agnosticity: wrap non-Bayesian inputs (gradient-boosted point models with predictive distributions) in Draws and verify blended ELPD, and check hierarchical-over-time weight behavior (weight migrates between models mid-season).
gate: Prototype on one backtest season: convert 3-5 existing models' outputs into Draws, fit MleStacking vs BayesStacking vs HierarchicalBayesStacking (covariate: week), and compare blended ELPD on leave-future-out weeks; validate .predict on unseen future weeks; ADOPT if blended ELPD beats the best single candidate on leave-future-out weeks AND weights agree with the manual pipeline of ledgers 1672-1673; REJECT if blending loses to the best candidate (the paper's own pseudo-BMA insurance result shows blending is not always the best).

title: Predictive Decision Synthesis for Portfolios: Betting on Better Models
improvement: Decision-tilted model combination for the weekly betting portfolio: define the GSE decision as the weekly portfolio of spread/moneyline/total bets sized by fractional Kelly from engine probabilities vs market prices; candidate set = engine model components/versions x stake-size/risk-target settings; replace the paper's decision score with realized Kelly log-growth (or ROI) on a selection window; apply relaxed entropic tilting to the BMA-style component weights to get decision-tilted combination weights; recompute tilted weights monthly from the picks history + historical odds (OddsPapi lane) - plus go beyond the paper: tilt on a risk-aware decision score the paper does not use - expected Kelly growth penalized by a drawdown term (growth - lambda*max-drawdown) - comparing relaxed-entropic-tilt, hard subset selection (their greedy 0.95 bar), and fully Bayesian decision-theoretic weighting.
gate: ADOPT the BPDS-tilted weights if 2025 holdout Kelly log-growth exceeds the accuracy-weighted baseline by >=10% relative (or ROI by >=1.0 point at matched stake) with a bootstrap p<0.05; REJECT otherwise; hard veto: if the tilted portfolio's worst-month drawdown exceeds the baseline's by >25%, reject regardless of full-season growth (decision-awareness must not smuggle tail risk).

title: Deep Learning and Transfer Learning Architectures for English Premier League Player Performance Forecasting
improvement: As engine-honesty infrastructure, keep the paper's 'points-only + matchup difficulty' feature-minimal 1D-CNN as a reference baseline: 1D-CNN forecaster for NFL week-ahead fantasy points (PPR), per position group (QB/RB/WR/TE): input = past w weeks of fantasy points (+ matchup difficulty from spread/total), single 1D conv layer -> flatten -> concat matchup difficulty -> one dense layer -> scalar output; MSE + ElasticNet loss, Adam, early stopping, player-wise splits; head-to-head vs GSE's current NFL projection baseline and vs LightGBM on the same features, evaluated on both MSE and Spearman rank correlation (the paper's key insight: ranking quality matters more than MSE for fantasy/prop selection) - plus direct Spearman optimization: train directly for ranking via convex-hull projection differentiable sorting instead of MSE, testing whether a rank-optimized model beats the MSE-optimized CNN on top-decile hit rate (fraction of predicted top-10 players finishing in the actual top-10).
gate: Adopt the 1D-CNN as a candidate NFL player projector if it beats the current engine's fantasy-points MSE by >=5% on holdout AND Spearman rho >= 0.55 in at least two position groups; if it merely ties LightGBM or fails to beat the current engine, reject and keep the paper as the feature-minimal baseline reference.

title: Delta Tensor: Efficient Vector and Tensor Storage in Delta Lake
improvement: Apply to the self-learning/self-growing engine mandate: (1) discovered-signal storage format - as the engine learns dense matchup embeddings or player-skill matrices, store them in Delta with FTSF-style chunking (id, chunk, dims metadata) rather than numpy/PyTorch blobs (buys the ~90% slice-read win for batch-time feature extraction - the 'fetch only this game's embeddings' pattern); (2) sparse interaction features (rare event tensors - trick plays, injuries per matchup): COO or CSF layout when nonzeros < 10%; (3) model checkpoint registry: store model weights as versioned Delta tables - time travel gives parameter history for free (pairs with ledger 2026's rollback story) - plus an access-log-driven auto-chunker: log which (week, team) slices the feature pipeline actually fetches over one season, then optimize chunk shape to minimize expected bytes-fetched (greedy search) - turning FTSF from a fixed layout into a learned layout.
gate: ADOPT the layout iff: (a) FTSF slice-read latency <= 25% of blob read-slice latency on GSE's season tensor; (b) write overhead <= 2x blob write; (c) exact numeric round-trip parity (decode(blob) == original to float32 precision); REJECT if slice reads do not beat blobs on GSE's smaller tensors.

title: Continual Learning in the Presence of Repetition
improvement: Frozen-expert ensemble over one forgetting monolith - NFL's stream is repetition-rich (divisional rematches, recurring coaching trees, repeated QB-vs-DC matchups): keep the live weekly-refit model (ledger 1888's interference-scored replay) as the 'current experience' expert, but maintain a bank of frozen specialist models: one per division (8), each trained only on that division's games through the prior season and frozen, plus one frozen 'rivalry/rematch' model trained on second-meetings; at inference, gate by OOD logic: each expert reports a confidence/OOD score for the matchup (distance of the game's features from its training distribution); final probability = reliability-weighted average, live model weighted by recency; cheap first step: before building 8 division experts, test (a) one weekly-refit monolith vs (b) monolith + frozen prior-season model (2-model ensemble, OOD-gated) on 2020-2025 walk-forward; add a 'rematch split' to the 1887 metric suite - report Brier separately on second-meetings vs first-meetings - plus learn the repetition structure: cluster historical games by matchup-embedding similarity (team-pair, coaching-tree, scheme tags) and train one frozen expert per cluster (e.g. 'Shanahan-tree vs Cover-3 teams'), cluster assignment refreshed each offseason.
gate: ADOPT the frozen-expert ensemble if on 2020-2025 walk-forward it beats the monolith on >=3 of the 4 metrics from 1887 with rematch-split Brier improving by >=0.003 and no metric degrading by >0.001; ADOPT the 2-model version (B) alone if it captures >=70% of (C)'s rematch gain at a fraction of the serving cost; REJECT the division bank if the shuffled-season control shows the same gains (then it is generic ensembling, not repetition exploitation); sunset rule: any frozen expert older than 2 seasons is retired unless it still wins its division split.

title: SoccerNet-Echoes: A Soccer Game Audio Commentary Dataset
improvement: Adapt the audio-commentary curation recipe to NFL: run Whisper large-v3 (best hallucination resistance) over full NFL broadcast audio per game; segment at segment-level timestamps; translate any non-English (Spanish broadcasts) to English; apply unique-word-ratio per-game model selection + VAD preprocessing; mine transcripts for (a) injury mentions and lineup changes (cross-validated against official reports), (b) mention-frequency-based player influence signals feeding summary/game-recap word budgets, (c) tactical-discussion extraction for coaching-adjustment signals; feed cleaned transcripts into the 1594-1597 text-event pipelines and the 1602 SoccerRAG-style QA layer - plus add VAD pre-processing + speaker diarization (separating commentators from crowd/stadium), entity linking to a player/team knowledge graph (fixes Whisper entity errors), segment-level (not batch) translation, and a human-verified injury-mention subset as a benchmark.
gate: ADAPT (not ADOPT): it is a data asset and curation recipe, not a predictive model; the transcription noise (WER ~0.5) means downstream extraction must be confidence-weighted; accepted on open dataset + code, honest quality metrics, hallucination-aware model selection, direct injury/tactical intelligence applications.

title: Assessing Course Difficulty and the Effect of Weather in Amateur Cross Country Running Races
improvement: Module weather/field_conditions.py: Bayesian log-scale mixed model for NFL weather/field-condition effects - log(total points) or log(team offensive yards) per game = lambda + alpha_offense_i + alpha_defense_j + beta_stadium_k + delta_week + gamma*(temp) + rho_0*(rain week of game) + rho_1*(rain prior 7 days) + dome/turf interactions; random effects for teams and stadiums, corner constraints, JAGS/Stan inference; the two-lag rainfall structure becomes game-day precipitation + trailing-7-day precipitation (field degradation), interacted with surface (grass vs turf); rain x temp interaction (frozen/saturated ground) and a wind x stadium-orientation term (bowl geometry); output: posterior distributions of weather/field effects per surface type -> calibrated totals adjustments (e.g. 'heavy trailing-week rain on grass: -1.5 points, 95% CI [-2.8, -0.3]') - with stadium-coordinate gridded reanalysis (replacing central-station weather to remove attenuation bias), and a hypothesis test: with stadium-level weather, wind shows an effect only in open, wind-aligned stadiums (Buffalo, Chicago), not domes or sheltered bowls.
gate: ADOPT the field-condition adjustment if (a) out-of-sample RMSE on 2025 totals improves >= 1.5% over the no-weather baseline, (b) trailing-week rain on grass has a 95% CI excluding zero with the correct sign, and (c) turf/dome rain effects are ~= 0; REJECT if weather terms add nothing out-of-sample.

title: Alternative ranking measures to predict international football results
improvement: Bayesian Bradley-Terry-Davidson strength covariate: fit Bayesian BTD in Stan/PyMC on nflverse 2002-2026 team-week W/L/T outcomes (no draws in NFL -> gamma->-infinity limit, or plain BT with home-field order effect via Beaver/Gokhale additive term): psi ~ N(0, sigma^2_psi), hierarchical sigma_psi estimated; posterior median psi_k per team per week using an expanding window (fit weekly, strengths as of that week - avoid the paper's pooled-window lookahead); feature: omega_n = MAD-normalized (psi_home - psi_away) added as a linear covariate to GSE's points/spread regression or as a model-blend input; dynamic extension: per-year AR(1) attack/defense adapted to offense/defense efficiency splits at week resolution - plus make the BTD strength time-varying within season via a state-space random walk psi_{k,t} ~ N(psi_{k,t-1}, sigma^2) (Glickman-style dynamic BT) with a score-differential (margin-of-victory) weighted likelihood (Stern/Harville style) so blowouts move strengths more than 1-point wins.
gate: ADOPT the covariate into the engine if, on the 2023-2025 walk-forward test, adding omega_n reduces moneyline Brier score by >=0.002 (paired, by week) AND does not worsen spread-cover Brier; REJECT (drop the feature) if the Brier delta is <0.001 in either direction or negative.

title: Expected Points Above Average: A Novel NBA Player Metric Based on Bayesian Hierarchical Modeling
improvement: Replicate the EPAA pipeline for NBA props: cluster players by shot-region selection and accuracy profiles (hierarchical Multinomial/Binomial), compute expected points at fixed usage N-tilde, define player EPAA vs league-average posterior; convert to betting: EPAA posterior -> expected points distribution for tonight's game (usage-adjusted); edge = E[points] - prop line; post only if edge > 0 and 95% credible interval excludes the line (ties to the 0714/0716 abstention gates); extend to other prop types: rebound/assist region profiles (analogous regions = court zones) - plus fix the paper's top-100 restriction: fit the hierarchical model on ALL rotation players with partial pooling (small-sample players - the paper's excluded set - are exactly where Bayesian shrinkage adds most value and where prop lines are softest); make the 'average' baseline time-varying (rolling 4-week average team) so EPAA tracks in-season regime change instead of a season-fixed baseline.
gate: ADOPT if the replicated EPAA pipeline shows positive backtest ROI on 2024-25 NBA props and EPAA-vs-line edge predicts covers better than the engine's current player model; REJECT if EPAA adds nothing over raw usage-adjusted averages.

title: Counterfactual Explanation-Based Badminton Motion Guidance Generation Using Wearable Sensors
improvement: Build gse_latentcf.py: (1) train a Transformer classifier on NGS tracking to predict play success (e.g., route -> target & catch, or ball-carrier -> broken tackle) from joint/position trajectories; (2) train a trajectory autoencoder on the same data; (3) for failed plays, run Algorithm 1 to generate the minimal counterfactual trajectory that flips the prediction to success; (4) two outputs: (a) @GalaxySportsHQ film-room content - ghost-overlay 'the 20 cm wider stem that makes this a completion'; (b) a counterfactual-gap feature per player (mean latent distance between actual and successful-counterfactual routes) fed into GSE's reception/prop models as a route-running quality signal orthogonal to raw athleticism - plus close the paper's open loop: content-side A/B testing whether film-room posts built on LatentCF counterfactuals outperform standard chart posts on engagement, validating that minimal-edit counterfactuals are the more compelling explanatory format.
gate: Reproduce Table II on MultiSenseBadminton (public): LatentCF must beat 1NN-DTW on DTW-closeness and FMD by >=25% relative; then port to NGS: train the success classifier on 2024 routes (gate: 5-fold BalAcc >= 0.70), generate counterfactuals for 200 failed routes, and gate on plausibility - mean LOF/OCSVM of CF trajectories within 1 SD of real successful routes; if CF trajectories are implausible (outside the real manifold), the explainer is unusable for content - stop.

title: An analysis of factors impacting team strengths in the Australian Football League using time-variant Bradley-Terry models
improvement: Time-variant Bradley-Terry with team random intercepts: nflverse play-by-play 2009-2025 (regular season); team-game-level differential features (off/def EPA differential last-4 and season-cumulative, success-rate differential, pressure-rate differential, turnover-margin differential, plus rest/travel days); target: ATS cover or straight-up win; model: logistic/Bradley-Terry with team random intercepts (epsilon_i ~ N(0, sigma^2)) fit via lme4/glmmTMB or PyMC; match-difficulty terms: home-field, rest differential, altitude/travel; ridge regularization over the PI differential coefficients (the paper's univariate screening + backward elimination is fragile); serving: weekly refit on a rolling 3-season window (the paper's 'medium-term drift' finding); output team strengths lambda_ir for downstream EPA opponent-adjustment and a calibrated win probability (add a Platt/calibration layer - the paper lacks one) - plus replace the feature screen with grouped elastic-net over the PI-differential blocks (EPA/SR/pressure/turnover blocks), add opponent-adjusted feature variants (iterated like EM), and model the spread margin with a team-effect linear model instead of win/loss.
gate: ADOPT if the BT time-variant model beats baseline (a) Elo on Brier score by >= 0.003 on the 2018-2025 test window AND matches or beats the closing-spread implied probability on log-loss; REJECT if it fails to beat Elo on Brier or trails the market by > 0.005 log-loss.

title: Multi Player Tracking in Ice Hockey with Homographic Projections
improvement: Adapt the homography+MPN tracking architecture to football (hockey model is not directly usable): (1) homography module: train or license an NFL-field registration model that maps broadcast frames to a top-down field template using field markings (yard lines, hash marks) as correspondences - deliverable: per-frame 3x3 H and per-player footpoints in field coordinates; (2) detection: fine-tune a detector (Faster R-CNN or YOLO variant) on football broadcast frames, with jersey-number OCR as an extra node feature (NFL advantage over hockey); (3) association: replicate the paper's bipartite-graph MPN: nodes = 512-D appearance + 2-D homography footpoints, edges = relative appearance/positional distances, L = 6 message-passing steps, focal-loss training, xi = 0.9 pruning, connected-component ID assignment; (4) training data: annotate an in-house football broadcast-tracking dataset (~80-100 clips) - no public equivalent of VIP-HTD exists for NFL; (5) serving: offline batch pipeline - ingest game footage -> tracklets -> bird's-eye positional trajectories -> feed into GSE's tracking-data consumers (NGS replacements, CFB games without tracking data) - plus jersey-number OCR as a node feature (near-deterministic identity signal), and camera-motion-compensated homography refinement (temporal smoothing on the H matrix sequence via Kalman filter) so pan/tilt/zoom jitter does not inject noise into footpoint trajectories.
gate: ADOPT the football adaptation only if ALL hold: (a) legal review clears processing of broadcast footage for the target sport/league (NFL excluded unless licensed - CFB or other leagues first); (b) a reproduction of the homography+MPN concept on public hockey data achieves IDF1 >= 90 with >=5 percentage-point gain over the appearance-only ablation; (c) an annotated football pilot set (>=10 games of broadcast clips) yields IDsw per game below a SORT-on-broadcast baseline by >=50%; reject otherwise - especially if legal review fails.

title: Modelling between- and within-season trajectories in elite athletic performance data
improvement: Decompose team form into between-season level and within-season trajectory: model each NFL team's weekly EPA/play (or GSE's rating) 2015-2025 as y_{team,season,week} = g(season-index) + f_{team,season}(week/18) + opponent/confounder terms, with f split into between-season level and within-season RBP - separating 'the Chiefs are declining as a roster' from 'the Chiefs start slow and peak in December'; player-prop age curves: fit the cubic B-spline population ageing function to position-level performance (QB EPA/dropback, WR yards/route by age) for age-adjustment in props - the reverse-J with position-specific peaks; replace Gaussian error assumptions with the asymmetric-tail skew-t (downside tail heavier - injuries -> sudden collapse is more likely than sudden superstar emergence); start with a non-Bayesian prototype (penalized likelihood) - plus build the forward-looking version: extend the model with a predictive distribution for the remaining within-season trajectory given weeks 1-k (the hierarchical prior naturally supports this - teams with few observations borrow from population/athlete-level curves), backtested at each week k=4..14 against GSE's current form estimator.
gate: Adopt the decomposition if the within-season trajectory component reduces second-half prediction MSE by >=5% vs the flat-season-average baseline on the 2015-2025 rolling test; reject if the gain is <2% (NFL's 17-game season may be too short for the within-season component to beat a simple recency-weighted average).

title: Sports-Traj: A Unified Trajectory Generation Model for Multi-Agent Movement in Sports
improvement: UniTraj for trajectory imputation + prediction on NFL Next Gen Stats tracking data - one model for GSE's three failure modes: partial tracking (occluded/missing frames), short-history rollout prediction (25-40 of 50 frames observed), fully-missing agents (dropped receiver ID); applications: (1) route/defender trajectory forecasting for EPA-added / separation features - generate 20 plausible continuations of all 22 players + ball from the first ~0.5 s of a play, deriving distributions of expected separation, YAC, tackle probability; (2) counterfactual play simulation - mask the ball-carrier's future, generate completions under different defensive masks (a generative complement to GSE's EPA models); (3) tracking-data QA - the OOB + Step metrics give an automatic quality gate for incoming NGS feeds; build plan: Phase 0 - reproduce the authors' code on Football-U (minADE20 within 5% of 3.55 yards); Phase 1 - NGS modern-schema data adapter - plus: variable agent counts (Perceiver-style latent bottleneck or padding-with-mask), replace the MLP decoder with a diffusion decoder for sharper cuts and better uncertainty calibration, add contextual conditioning the paper omits (down, distance, score differential, personnel grouping, weather).
gate: ADOPT only if UniTraj beats GSE's Kalman-filter rollout baseline by >= 15% on minADE20 with OOB < 1e-03 on time-ordered NGS (train 2023-2024, test 2025 weeks 1-4) over the paper's prediction masks; ADAPT (imputation-only use) if it wins only on imputation masks; otherwise REJECT.

title: Causal-ICM: Multi-task Gaussian Processes for Combining RCT and Observational Data
improvement: Two-source GP combining GSE's trusted pick outcomes with large biased historical model outputs: source A = GSE's own verified pick outcomes (small, trusted, post-hoc verified - the picks DB); source B = large historical model outputs (biased: stale, miscalibrated eras); shared RBF kernel on game-state covariates (spread, total, rest, weather); single global rho first, then region-specific rho via a second ICM factor; gpytorch with inducing points (<=500) for ~10k rows; rho grid {0.1,...,0.9} via rolling-origin time-split CV on source-A outcomes only (never tune rho on source B - that reintroduces the confounding the parameter is meant to absorb); output per-pick: posterior mean edge and the bound-inflated posterior variance -> feed into calibration (Venn-Abers/isotonic) and Kelly sizing rather than point picks - plus region-adaptive rho: rho(x) = sigmoid(g(x)) with g a second GP or linear model on covariates, so borrowing shrinks where source B is known to be unreliable (stale-rating eras, weather-affected totals).
gate: ADOPT if: on the 2026 holdout, Causal-ICM beats pooled-GP Brier by >=0.005 on all picks AND by >=0.01 on the out-of-support slice, with rho-hat selected by rolling CV stable across folds (SD of rho-hat <= 0.15); REJECT if rho-hat collapses to ~=0 or ~=1, or if any baseline (pooled GP or engine) beats it on total Brier.

title: Expected Possession Value of Control and Duel Actions for Soccer Player's Skills Estimation
improvement: Build an NFL 'Expected Drive Value' (EDV) framework: data = nflverse play-by-play 2018-2025; possession = drive, control actions = plays, 'shots' = scoring plays (TD/FG) with xP (expected points) replacing xG; fit drive-value models: per-play EDV = 1 - Pi(1 - gamma^Delta-t * xP_future) with gamma per-second-of-game-clock tuned ~0.90-0.99 on the drive length distribution; possession-risk variant subtracting opponent's next-drive decayed xP; player attribution: per-play Delta-EDV credited to the primary actor (passer/receiver split 60/40 per GSE convention; rusher full), turnovers penalized double; duel-skill analog: contested-catch and pass-rush/win rates via modified Glicko-2; custom loss: weight each play's loss by 1/(player appearance count) when fitting projection models for low-volume/deep-roster players - plus replace the ad hoc gamma with a learned per-situation discount: fit gamma as a function of field position and down (early-down midfield plays decay faster since drives routinely die there; red-zone plays decay slower).
gate: ADAPT into GSE's player-projection pipeline only if: (a) EDV-based next-season prediction achieves the R^2 gains on 2023 AND 2024 holdout seasons, and (b) the Glicko-2 contested-catch rating shows rank stability (Spearman >= 0.45 year-over-year for players with >=30 contested targets); otherwise park as research.

title: SoccerRAG: Multimodal Soccer Information Retrieval via Natural Queries
improvement: Port the pipeline to NFL: (a) structured SQLite/Postgres DB of GSE's archive - games, play-by-play, rosters, injuries, odds/CLV history, commentary transcripts (Whisper on Game Pass audio, mirroring the paper's ASR step); (b) extractor schema for NFL properties (team, player, week, season, stat, market); (c) validator with NFL abbreviation tables ('KC', 'Mahomes', 'MNF') + Levenshtein resolution - the paper's ablation proves the validator is the component to build first; (d) few-shot SQL RAG with human-crafted exemplar queries for common GSE questions (splits, line-movement, injury-report lookups); (e) expose as the natural-language query interface behind @GalaxySportsHQ content research and the engine's internal analytics - plus swap GPT-3.5/4 for a modern function-calling open model and re-run the 20-question ablation; add a determinism/robustness metric (5 repeated runs per question); fix list-truncation with paginated SQL + structured output; measure validator recall on deliberately misspelled/abbreviated NFL entity queries; extend to multimodal retrieval (return video clips keyed to event timestamps).
gate: ACCEPTED (ADAPT): open-source reproducible pipeline + controlled ablation isolating the validator's contribution + honest failure documentation; ADAPT rather than ADOPT: soccer schema/LLM choices are dated - reimplement with current open models and GSE's NFL schema.

title: Leveraging Deterministic Weather Forecasts for In-Situ Probabilistic Temperature Predictions via Deep Learning
improvement: Calibrated probabilistic kickoff-condition forecasts: data = deterministic high-res forecast grids (HRRR/NAM) at 30 NFL stadiums + ASOS/METAR obs; steps: (a) build the 25-style predictor set for wind speed, gusts, temperature, precip at kickoff lead times; (b) train one BQN (d = 16) with stadium + lead-time embeddings on all lead times jointly; (c) output per-stadium calibrated quantile functions for kickoff conditions; (d) pipe into the totals/spread weather adjustment model - plus add ensemble members (GEFS) as extra inputs (the paper shows the 2nd member is the high-value one) and test CRPS gains vs the deterministic-only BQN; extend Bernstein degree by validation and add an EVT tail model for extreme cold/heat games (the Texas-2021 failure mode).
gate: ADAPT if the BQN achieves >=10% relative CRPS improvement over the naive probabilistic baseline on a holdout season AND rank histograms are flatter (central-bin deviation from uniformity reduced by >=30%); otherwise fall back to EMOS.

title: Decision Synthesis in Monetary Policy
improvement: Decision-utility weighting for the GSE ensemble: (1) component predictive densities: each sub-model j produces p_j(y|x) over game outcomes y given a candidate action x (stake profile across spread/total/moneyline, or a slate of picks); (2) decision-dependent weights pi_j(x): weight each sub-model by its historical betting utility - realized CLV or ROI of the picks it would have recommended - with weights varying by bet type/market (a totals model gets more weight on totals decisions); (3) outcome calibration alpha_j(y|x): upweight models in outcome regions where they excel (a model strong in high-total games gets upweighted when the predicted total is high); (4) bounded score functions on (predicted edge, bankroll drawdown, stake smoothness) with entropic tilting to a target expected score per slate; monitor importance-sampling ESS as a feasibility check (if ESS collapses, the target is unrealistic - shrink it); final pick: x maximizing expected utility under the BPDS mixture - plus make pi_j(x) depend on the market state (line movement, public-betting splits) as well as bet type, and replace the hand-set target scores m_f(x) with an adaptive rule driven by the ESS diagnostic (shrink targets when ESS < 50).
gate: Adopt decision-utility weighting if walk-forward 2024-2025 shows the BPDS-weighted ensemble beating predictive-fit-weighted (BMA-style) combination by >=1.0% ROI or >=0.5% CLV with no worse max drawdown; reject (keep current combination) if decision-utility weights underperform - the paper's own caveat: if historical decisions were bad, weighting by past decision outcomes fossilizes the mistake; use expected decision utility under a corrected staking rule instead.

title: Online Learning in Betting Markets: Profit versus Prediction
improvement: Defensive book-shading monitor: given GSE's own released picks flow as a proxy for informed-bettor beliefs, use the paper's profit-decomposition (profit proportional to deviation between bettor beliefs and truth, amplified by tail heaviness) to predict when books will move lines against GSE-style positions - time GSE's releases/picks to precede anticipated shading, or flag markets where the book's margin already prices in the informed flow (no edge left); benchmark: implement the fair-odds FTL price a-star (eq. 27) as a 'market-consensus' baseline - compare GSE's model probabilities against the FTL-implied consensus from a simulated crowd, persistent deviations indicate either GSE edge or model bias; simulation lab: reuse the authors' repo to simulate how a book would price against a population of GSE-like Kelly bettors, stress-testing GSE's staking plan against adversarial pricing dynamics - plus invert the model: have GSE learn the bookmaker's belief g from the observed price path (inverse SA) - estimate g per market from opening->closing line movement, then compare implied g against GSE's model probability as a direct edge-detection signal.
gate: ADAPT the shading-monitor if, on one full NFL season, games flagged 'book already shaded against informed flow' show GSE's realized CLV >=2 points worse than unflagged games (the flag correctly identifies dead-edge spots); otherwise REJECT the defensive application and keep only the FTL-consensus benchmark.

title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
improvement: Adapt TextGrad to optimize the signal-discovery pipeline itself: graph: SignalCode = LLM(IdeaPrompt + SignalHypothesis) -> BacktestResult = Executor(SignalCode) -> Loss = -DeltaBrier(BacktestResult) (deterministic - NOT an LLM judge); variables with requires_grad: IdeaPrompt, SignalCode; backward: a backward-engine LLM receives the backtest diagnostics (which folds failed, sample sizes, calibration slope - the structured evaluator output from 2084) as the 'gradient' on BacktestResult, producing criticisms for SignalCode ('the wind interaction fails because...') AND for IdeaPrompt ('hypotheses about weather need a minimum-games guard...'); chain rule = one backward call per edge; TGD.step: update SignalCode and IdeaPrompt with the Eq.-9-style prompt; 5 iterations max per idea (paper's budget); minibatch mode: batch 4 ideas, tg.sum their losses, concatenate gradients - improves the IdeaPrompt across ideas, not just one; effort: 2-3 days (Variable/graph wrapper around the 2082/2084 harness) - plus a gradient-clip analogue: cap each TGD.step to changing at most K lines of SignalCode / K tokens of IdeaPrompt per iteration (like gradient clipping in SGD), testing whether clipped steps reduce the variance of DeltaBrier across the 5 iterations and raise the fraction of ideas that monotonically improve.
gate: ADOPT if: arm B clears the 0.002 gate on >=5/8 ideas vs <=3/8 for arm A, AND the transferred IdeaPrompt improves first-attempt DeltaBrier on the 4 held-out hypotheses by >=0.001 on average (the prompt itself is learning - the TextGrad value-add over Reflexion), AND total LLM calls per idea <= 20; REJECT if arm B ~= arm A (joint optimization adds nothing over single reflection), or the IdeaPrompt drifts into prompt-bloat, or any iteration's 'gradient' contradicts the deterministic backtest numbers (backward engine hallucinating - fall back to 2084's simpler reflection).

title: Tractable Ridge Regression for Paired Comparisons
improvement: PEB-ridge for early-season paired-comparison ratings: on the NFL 2019-2023 early-season protocol (train weeks 1-6, predict weeks 7-17), with the closed-form lambda-hat; if the lambda-hat closed form underperforms full PEB on NFL data, use full PEB - plus build a dynamic PEB where lambda_t evolves via a random walk (or is re-estimated on a rolling window) so shrinkage adapts to within-season regime changes (injuries, QB changes), tested on the 2022-2023 NFL seasons with known mid-season QB injuries (dynamic-PEB log-loss vs static-PEB on post-injury weeks); extend the concordance-based lambda-hat to the spread domain by correlating paired ATS outcomes instead of paired SU outcomes.
gate: On the NFL 2019-2023 early-season protocol (train weeks 1-6, predict weeks 7-17), PEB-ridge log-loss must be <= GSE current early-season rating log-loss - 0.01, and must beat the naive frequency baseline by >= 0.05 in every season; if PEB ties CV-ridge within noise, adopt PEB for the compute savings.

title: Modeling cyclicality and intransitivity in paired comparisons data
improvement: Cycle-aware paired-comparison diagnostics for NFL: deploy the cyclic pipeline as a monitoring diagnostic - lack-of-fit flags at p < 0.01 on walk-forward seasons; extend FTBS to incomplete graphs (NFL: 17 games/team, not round-robin) - the tick-table machinery needs the incidence-matrix generalization the authors defer - and test detection power on simulated NFL-like schedules with planted cycles; longer cycles (r >= 4) as first-class dictionary entries for interpretability ('A beats B beats C beats D beats A' narratives for content).
gate: Deploy the cyclic pipeline to production only if, on EPL 2022-2024 walk-forward: (i) lack-of-fit flags >= 1 season at p < 0.01; (ii) FTBS-augmented model beats the transitive baseline by >= 0.005 log-loss on flagged-season holdout; (iii) the cyclic-edge betting simulation shows positive expected gain net of vig; otherwise keep the test as a monitoring diagnostic (cheap) without acting on it.
